axes.model_access: The platform natively connects to the Gemini model family and can reach third-party models via Model Garden; the official page (fetched directly 2026-10-21) shows the product line folded into the "Gemini platform" narrative (Innovate, build, and deploy enterprise-ready agents).
axes.runtime: Cloud-hosted: agents run on Google Cloud (Vertex/Agentspace lines); no self-hosted form.
axes.local_files: Data sources connect to in-cloud connectors such as BigQuery/Drive/SharePoint; it hosts no local-file runtime.
axes.background: Cloud-hosted residency is the default form: the agent service stays online with the GCP deployment, triggers and scheduling carried by the platform; "keeps running when your laptop is off" naturally holds in the hosted form. No official statement of a self-hosted form.
axes.tools: Official component/extension library + function calling + data connectors; MCP support status not verified item by item.
axes.context: Sessions and retrieval (RAG/grounding) are the official context main axis; cross-session memory not verified item by item.
axes.permissions: IAM/organization policies follow the Google Cloud system; data-residency options follow the GCP region model.
axes.fit: Fits: GCP-installed enterprises, the Gemini-native stack, governance ready-made. Does not fit: outside the GCP ecosystem; self-hosting.

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The closest test protocol is the code-side [protocols/framework/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/framework/_protocol.md) (the tool-calling and credential-boundary sections are reusable; no workflow-platform-specific protocol exists on this site yet).
unknowns:
- The current product-line naming (the relationship among Agent Builder / Gemini Enterprise / Agentspace — the official page narrative drifts; only what direct fetching showed is recorded)
- MCP support status (no official documentation found)
- The complete list of third-party model connections
related: Two legs of the same family: ADK writes code, Agent Builder drags a UI, and both land on Google Cloud runtimes.
